problem.title: You've Built the Wealth. You Just Don't Have a *Real Income Plan.*

items.title: A Pile Of Accounts
items.body: Your retirement "plan" is a stack of 401(k)s, IRAs, and brokerage accounts with a vague target date — no real income strategy and no proof it survives a downturn.

items.title: Sequence-Of-Returns Risk
items.body: If a major market drop hits right as you retire, you could be forced to sell low — and a 50% loss needs a 100% gain just to recover. Most people have no idea how much risk they are actually carrying.

items.title: Fees, Taxes & No Coordination
items.body: You suspect you're overpaying in fees and taxes — getting generic portfolio management with zero coordination across tax, insurance, estate, and income.

problem.transition: The biggest retirement risks show up *over years, not weeks* — and they're decided before you retire, not after.

items.title: A Reliable Retirement Paycheck
items.body: A clear “paycheck vs. playcheck” plan — guaranteed income for your essentials and flexible income for the extras — designed to stay steady even in down markets.

items.title: Lower Fees & Smarter Risk

items.body: Access to options like principal-protected structured notes and non-correlated assets, with your plan stress-tested for a bad market early in retirement.

faqs.q: I already have a financial advisor. Why do I need this?
faqs.a: Most clients do. The difference is coordination: we stress-test your income, audit fees and taxes, and tie investments, insurance, and estate together — the questions a "money manager" rarely answers.

faqs.q: Is this a sales pitch for products?
faqs.a: No. We're fiduciaries. The assessment and review are educational; any recommendation is based on what's right for your plan, never a commission.

faqs.q: What is the Retirement Red Zone Stress Test?
faqs.a: It shows how your accounts and withdrawal plan would hold up if a major market drop hit early in retirement — so you understand your real risk before it matters.

faqs.q: How much do I need to get started?
faqs.a: We typically work with households with $2M–$10M in investable assets, though the right fit always depends on your specific situation and goals.

faqs.q: What does being a fiduciary mean?
faqs.a: We're legally and ethically required to act in your best interest — coordinating your full plan rather than selling products.

faqs.q: How quickly will someone follow up?
faqs.a: If you qualify, a fiduciary specialist typically reaches out within one business day to schedule your strategy session.

faqs.q: How can you reduce risk without giving up growth?
faqs.a: Through true diversification — combining non-correlated assets and, when appropriate, options like principal-protected structured notes — paired with risk analysis that targets your portfolio’s real drawdown, not just its average return.

faqs.q: What is the “paycheck vs. playcheck” approach?
faqs.a: We split your retirement income into a guaranteed “paycheck” for essentials (from sources like annuities and income notes layered on Social Security and pensions) and a flexible “playcheck” for discretionary spending — so your core lifestyle is protected in any market.
